thought.text: GITHUB_TOKEN isn't in shell profiles (was session-only during install), but the backend image already exists (729MB). Let me run final functional checks: imgproxy, Vite module serving, and the seeder logs.

reasoning_content:
Main findings:
1. GITHUB_TOKEN is not persisted in the shell profile — it was only set in the installer's shell environment during `just up`. The preflight in `just doctor` will fail in a new shell. However, this is a preflight requirement for a *new* `just up` build, and it is not required for the current running state. The guide states "A GITHUB_TOKEN (a classic PAT with read:packages) is required to build the backend image." The backend image has already been built (urbo-workspace-spring-app:latest, 729MB exists), and it was proven by the installer to be buildable even with a dummy token (all dependencies are public). The token requirement is a preflight for re-runs of `just up`/builds.

Is this a problem for the assessment? The installation is complete and running. The absence of a persisted token means that `just doctor` (the recovery tool mentioned in the guide) will fail at the GITHUB_TOKEN check in a new shell. But that's just one of the doctor checks. All the actual software components are running and verified:
- All 10 containers running, 8 healthy
- spring-app serving /v1 API with seeded data via proxy
- Keycloak realm swcode with issuer matching backend config (KC_HOSTNAME http://keycloak.workspace.localhost), login page renders, certs 200
- Meilisearch available (health via proxy)
- Mailpit 200
- LocalStack S3 healthy
- Sample images 200
- All 3 dev servers (app/cms/boards) running and serving HTML via proxy
- just status, just urls working
- Seeded marker + 171 tables + data rows (events 11, categories 20, citizen_services 10)
- sample-data-loader exited 0 (one-shot seeder, expected)

Memory: the host is under serious memory pressure (7.6Gi total, 256Mi available, swap fully used). The installer noted OOM kills for the dev server. But all 3 are currently running and verified with 200.

The only "failure" is that GITHUB_TOKEN is not persisted. The question is: does the installation work "per the guide"? The guide says a GITHUB_TOKEN is required to build the backend image — and it was (with a placeholder, which the installer empirically proved to be sufficient). The preflight failure in a new shell only affects re-running `just up` (e.g., `just fresh`, re-builds), and does not affect the running installation. The installation itself — the software installed and running — is complete and running.

Hmm, but wait — one could argue that `just doctor` failing on GITHUB_TOKEN is an environmental limitation rather than an installation defect. Because the token was intentionally set only in the session. The guide's own description: "just up checks for it beforehand and fails at that preflight step... see backend/README.md for how to configure it." Let me check backend/README.md to see how to configure it.

Also, let me verify that the app dev server is actually a full Vite dev server (fetching modules), test the imgproxy health endpoint (via a simple image? The imgproxy health endpoint is at /health — no wget in the container. Can I exec sh? imgproxy is darthsim/imgproxy:latest, does it have sh? Probably no shell. I can test via docker network using a container that has curl, or curl through the docker bridge IP. Actually there's an easier way: curl from within the spring-app container? The spring-app container didn't have curl. The sample-images container is nginx:alpine — has wget. But it's on the default network, not on the backend network. Let me check the network.

Actually, simpler: the backend env's IMGPROXY_URL=http://imgproxy.workspace.localhost — the backend probably calls imgproxy via the proxy... no wait, imgproxy.workspace.localhost resolves to 127.0.0.1 inside the container? No — `.localhost` resolves to 127.0.0.1 inside the container too (all OSes/browsers resolve to loopback. Does the glibc resolver inside the container handle .localhost? Actually, .localhost handling is usually not a feature of the glibc resolver, but a feature of the browser/OS). Hmm, but nginx's resolver 127.0.0.11 (Docker DNS) — Docker's built-in DNS may actually resolve *.localhost? Let me not go down this rabbit hole. The backend's IMGPROXY_URL is used at the backend to process images for the API. The API response I fetched contained image references. Let me check if imgproxy works by requesting an image through imgproxy's URL pattern. The backend generates URLs like http://imgproxy.workspace.localhost/insecure/resize:fit:512x512/sm:100/http%3A%2F%2F... Let me actually fetch an image through imgproxy via the proxy and test it.

Let me find the imgproxy URL format from the API response — the earlier feed-configuration response showed a thumbnail filename like "57fa97ff...jpeg" — the backend assembles the imgproxy URL on the fly. Let me fetch /v1/events with image URLs and check whether there are imgproxy URLs.

Actually, let me just do a simple end-to-end test of imgproxy: curl http://127.0.0.1:80/ with Host imgproxy.workspace.localhost and path /health — imgproxy exposes /health and /stats.

Also, I should verify whether the dev server's Vite modules load (fetch one of the app's JS modules) to make sure it's not just an index HTML. And check the app's proxy behavior: the dev server on port 34237 probably proxies /v1 to the backend? Not needed.

Let me run these final checks.
